claims.claim: What did the Great Pyramid look like in Cleopatra's day? Not this. (said over a photograph of the pyramid as it is now)
claims.source_checked: Diodorus 1 (Oldfather, Loeb vol. I, 1933) on LacusCurtius, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Diodorus_Siculus/1C*.html (1.63.5); Herodotus 2.124-125 (Godley 1920) on Perseus, https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0126%3Abook%3D2%3Achapter%3D124 (2.124.5); frames 0-160 in out/review/factcheck12/ (2 fps full-size frames in full/, every frame around each cut in trans/)
claims.note: Hook (A4). The line asserts only that it looked different; that rests on Herodotus 'the whole is of stone polished and most exactly fitted' and Diodorus 'the stones remain to this day still preserving their original position and the entire structure undecayed', both read. 'In Cleopatra's day', not 'Cleopatra saw' (A5). SOURCES 1 quotes the line exactly. Unsure point, not a fault: for the first 3.7 s the present-day photo sits under the label 'In Cleopatra's day?' and the 'Today' label only arrives at about 3.9 s; it is a question, so nothing false is asserted, but 'Today' from frame 0 would be safer for a viewer who swipes at 2 s.

claims.claim: It still wore its smooth, polished outer casing.
claims.source_checked: Herodotus 2.124-125 (Godley 1920) on Perseus, https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.01.0126%3Abook%3D2%3Achapter%3D124 (2.124.5); Diodorus 1 (Oldfather, Loeb vol. I, 1933) on LacusCurtius, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Diodorus_Siculus/1C*.html (1.63.4-5 and Loeb n. 53); Tallet & Marouard 2014 full text, https://archive.org/download/theharborofkhufuontheredseacoastatwadialjarfegypt/ (the _djvu.txt file) p. 10
claims.note: Herodotus (5th c. BC): 'of stone polished and most exactly fitted'. Diodorus, who visited in 60-56 BC: 'the stones remain to this day still preserving their original position and the entire structure undecayed', and the pyramid 'tapers to the top, where each side is six cubits long'. Tallet & Marouard: Tura blocks 'were probably used for the external casing of the Great Pyramid, made of fine limestone'. All three quotations in SOURCES 2 are in the sources as quoted. Unsure point: no 1st-century-BC source read uses the word 'polished'; 'still polished' is an inference from Herodotus plus Diodorus's 'undecayed'. I accept it under A3 because the line describes the casing that was polished as still being worn, which Diodorus supports.

claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to its building.
claims.source_checked: Rosso 2021, PMC8042289 full text (NCBI BioC API); NASA Image Library record AS11-40-5903, https://images-api.nasa.gov/search?q=AS11-40-5903; Erdil et al. 2025 S2 Table, https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?type=supplementary&id=10.1371/journal.pone.0314612.s005; Sheisha et al. 2022, PMC9477388 full text (NCBI BioC API); script/cleopatra-timeline.txt SOURCES 1-5
claims.note: Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC'. NASA: AS11-40-5903 dated 20 July 1969. 69 BC to AD 1969 = 2,037 years (no year zero). Erdil S2 Table: Djedefra's accession (end of Khufu's reign) median 2565, 2577, 2586, 2603, 2603 BC across the five models, so 2,496-2,534 years before 69 BC. Sheisha lists Khufu's accession as 2613-2577, 2589, 2554 or 2480 +/- 5 BCE: even on the lowest the pyramid is about 2,390 years before her birth, more than 2,037. Holds on every chronology read.

Born 69 BC (Rosso; the Berlin museum record also says 'im Jahr 69 v. Chr. ... geboren'), so she was about 9 to 13.

claims.claim: He wrote that its stones were still in place.
claims.source_checked: Diodorus 1 (Oldfather, Loeb vol. I, 1933) on LacusCurtius, https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/E/Roman/Texts/Diodorus_Siculus/1C*.html (1.63.2, 1.63.5, Loeb n. 52)

The statement is Diodorus's own, not hearsay ('as they say' attaches only to the count of years).
